title: Middle of the Linked List
statement: Return the middle node of a singly linked list (the values from that node to the end are compared). If there are two middle nodes, return the second one.

hints.1_question: If one person walks twice as fast as another, where is the slow one when the fast one finishes?
hints.2_nudge: Use two pointers starting at head. Move slow by 1 and fast by 2 each round.
hints.3_big_hint: Loop while fast and fast.next: slow = slow.next; fast = fast.next.next. Return slow.

known_bugs.name: returns the first middle for even lengths
known_bugs.followup: For a list of 4 nodes, which of the two middle nodes does your code return? Which does the problem want?

known_bugs.name: crashes when fast runs off the end
known_bugs.followup: When the list has an even length, what is `fast` after its last jump, and what happens when you read fast.next?

known_bugs.name: returns the node after the middle
known_bugs.followup: Trace a one-node list. What does your function return?

followups: Why is this one pass instead of two (count, then walk)? Is it actually faster?
How would you return the first middle instead, and which loop condition changes?
